_comment: Geometry in the XLeRobot URDF's base_link frame: origin on the FLOOR at the
cart's centre, +x forward, +y to the robot's LEFT, +z up.
Nearly everything here is now taken from the project's own full-robot URDF
rather than estimated. Each entry says SOURCED or ESTIMATE.
Validation still worth doing: probe_range.py recorded the shoulder_pan
angles at which each arm actually met the tower; a correct model must
predict collisions at roughly those angles.

_sources.full_robot_urdf: Vector-Wangel/XLeRobot simulation/Maniskill/assets/xlerobot/xlerobot.urdf -- the complete robot: both arms, both wrist cameras, head pan/tilt. Authoritative; supersedes the earlier photograph estimates.
_sources.arm_mounts: arm_base_joint / arm_base_joint_2: xyz -0.135 -/+0.133 0.760, rpy 0 0 90deg. The arm at y=-0.133 carries Right_Arm_Camera and the one at y=+0.133 carries Left_Arm_Camera -- independently confirming +y = the robot's LEFT, established on hardware from a mechanical stop plus FK (lex-robot#163).
_sources.tower: top_base_joint puts top_base_link at z=0.73; head_pan_joint offsets x=-0.178; head_tilt_joint sits 0.43815 above it. The mast runs z=0.73 to 1.168 at x=-0.178 -- 43 mm BEHIND the arm bases, which the earlier estimate had at the same x.
_sources.cart: IKEA RASKOG, article 40582181, from XLeRobot's bill of materials. Published 35 x 45 x 78 cm, 3 tiers; the 0.760 arm-mount height is consistent with the 0.78 m cart.
_sources.radii: NOT published. Link radii and mast radius remain estimates; the URDF carries meshes, not primitives.
_sources.arm_yaw: DERIVED, not sourced. The two URDFs use different arm base frames, so xlerobot.urdf's rpy does not transfer. yaw=0 was chosen because it is the only quarter-turn that makes the arms symmetric and forward-reaching. Worth confirming against a measured gripper position before trusting arm-vs-arm results.

left._provenance: Position SOURCED from xlerobot.urdf's arm_base_joint_2. Yaw is 0, NOT the 90deg that URDF states: that 90deg is expressed in XLeRobot's own arm frame (Base/Rotation_Pitch/Upper_Arm), which is rotated relative to the so101_new_calib.urdf this model does FK with. Applying 90deg here sends both grippers to +y (left tip y=+0.524, right y=+0.258 -- both arms pointing the same way across the robot), which is impossible for a symmetric build. yaw=0 is the only value giving a symmetric forward-reaching pair, left (+0.256,+0.133) and right (+0.256,-0.133).

right._provenance: Position SOURCED from xlerobot.urdf's arm_base_joint. Yaw is 0, NOT the 90deg that URDF states: that 90deg is expressed in XLeRobot's own arm frame (Base/Rotation_Pitch/Upper_Arm), which is rotated relative to the so101_new_calib.urdf this model does FK with. Applying 90deg here sends both grippers to +y (left tip y=+0.524, right y=+0.258 -- both arms pointing the same way across the robot), which is impossible for a symmetric build. yaw=0 is the only value giving a symmetric forward-reaching pair, left (+0.256,+0.133) and right (+0.256,-0.133).

tower._provenance: SOURCED position and height from head_pan_joint + head_tilt_joint; radius is an ESTIMATE.

cart._provenance: SOURCED -- IKEA RASKOG 35 x 45 x 78 cm; arms bolt to the top tray at z=0.760.

link_radii._provenance: ESTIMATE -- conservative capsules enclosing each link plus sleeve and cabling. Keyed by the link a capsule ENDS at.
